Agreed next steps include checklist share, pilot SOW, and an on-site sizing call.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-01-09 14:30 EST
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Marta Li, Derek O'Connell, Priya Raman (Redwood) - Dr. Saira Khan, Michael Reyes, Anika Bose, Leo Zhang (Northern Pathology Labs)

Summary (auto): Discussed feasibility of airlocked on-prem deployment, update workflows, hardware limits, and compliance needs.

[00:00] Marta Li: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time. I'm Marta from Redwood, AE on this. Welcome. Quick intros?
[00:12] Dr. Saira Khan: Hi, I'm Saira, CTO at Northern Pathology. We're migrating a few inference workloads from cloud to an on-prem, airlocked node for compliance.
[00:21] Michael Reyes: Michael, infra lead, I manage on-site racks and networking.
[00:25] Anika Bose: Anika, compliance. I handle HIPAA and CLIA controls.
[00:29] Leo Zhang: Leo, site ops, power and cooling.
[00:33] Derek O'Connell: Derek, SE, I'll do the technical walkthrough and capture constraints.
[00:38] Marta Li: Great. High level, we want to understand your success criteria, timeline, and blockers so we can map to Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private — but I know for you Private air-gapped is the primary path. Can you share the why?
[00:51] Dr. Saira Khan: Sure, the labs process PHI. We need to ensure there's no egress, and regular audits require physical separation. Cloud is not an option for primary workload. We also need reproducible audit trails and signed binaries for any code that runs on the system.
[01:08] Michael Reyes: Also our datacenter is older. We have racks with 2x 42U cages, limited PDUs — some PDUs are older 20A circuits. We mostly run older gen GPUs, a couple of A40s and a mix of T4s. No NVLink in most racks.\n[01:30] Derek O'Connell: Okay, that matters for throughput and for whether we recommend multi-GPU model parallel. NVLink absence changes memory sharing and KV cache approaches. Quick question: are you planning to run model weights fully on GPU or do you want CPU-backed quantized execution for some models?
[01:43] Michael Reyes: Ideally GPU for the heavier models for latency, but cost wise we may choose 8-bit quantized variants that fit 48GB memory.
[01:52] Marta Li: Noted. On updates: we typically provide a signed bundle containing runtime, model artifacts, and a packaging manifest. For air-gapped installs you can transfer via secure media and verify signature via on-prem KMS or local HSM. Is there an HSM on site or a KMS requirement?
[02:08] Anika Bose: We have an HSM router in the compliance room but it’s limited. We need recommendations for integrating Redwood's signing or supporting customer-side key stores. Also retention for logs should be 7 years for some traceability per our auditors.
[02:25] Priya Raman: We support both customer-managed KMS and Redwood-managed signing keys. For offline verification we can include a delta patcher with a signature check and an audit manifest. Our offline installer writes to /var/log/redwood and we can pipe logs to your internal S3-like object store or WORM storage.
[02:43] Leo Zhang: Is that WORM S3 like our on-prem object? We're using an older Ceph cluster for archival; it supports immutability.
[02:50] Priya Raman: That should work, we just need an endpoint to drop the compressed signed audit bundles.
[02:55] Marta Li: Let's dig into the update cadence — what's your ideal window?
[02:59] Anika Bose: We can do quarterly security updates, but model updates must be auditable and only after validation in a staging isolated network. So we want a signed bundle, staging verification, then a maintenance window for applying. No automatic outbound check-ins allowed.
[03:15] Derek O'Connell: Good — we can do a manual apply workflow. Typical flow: Redwood generates signed artifact -> security reviews -> transfer via USB/air-gapped transfer -> run local verification tool that checks signature against your HSM CA -> perform dry-run on staging -> apply on production with snapshotting. We'll provide scripts and a verification binary.
[03:34] Michael Reyes: That binary needs to run on RHEL 7 and 8; our infra is mixed. Also we might have to run the verifiers on an isolated jump box.
[03:43] Derek O'Connell: We support RHEL 7/8 for the verifier. We'll include checksums, GPG-like signatures plus optional HSM PKCS#11 support.
[03:52] Dr. Saira Khan: About model sizes — we run a 13B encoder for de-id plus a 7B note summarizer. Latency target for clinical workflow is sub-400ms p50 on the 13B for single request in peak times, and 95th under 1.2s. Can that be achieved on an A40 or T4?
[04:11] Derek O'Connell: T4s will struggle for that 13B at low tail latency. A40s might be okay with quantization and optimized kernels; but without NVLink multi-GPU becomes more about batching and model sharding which increases latency. For strict p50 under 400ms, we recommend at least one A100 or equivalent per model service or using an optimized 8-bit quantized runtime with larger GPU memory.
[04:31] Michael Reyes: A100s are a no-go in current racks due to power draw; upgrade is a project. Is there a middle-ground like using CPU+GPU hybrid or lower-latency batching?
[04:41] Derek O'Connell: Hybrid can work — smaller models on GPU, CPU for background batch jobs. We can also suggest model distillation or 8-bit quantization to reduce footprint. Redwood Optimize can run offline evals to recommend quant profiles given your workloads. That would be part of the pilot.
[04:58] Marta Li: Let's talk about network constraints — you said no egress. Do you have an internal registry for packages or do we need to ship sealed USBs?
[05:07] Michael Reyes: No internal registry that's allowable for external access. We have a secure build pipeline but artifact transfer must be via physical media and checks.
[05:14] Priya Raman: We can provide signed tarballs and a transfer checklist. We also support a 'sneakernet' install path — we document step-by-step. For telemetry, we support toggling to full-offline mode where the agent never attempts to reach Redwood and all telemetry is local.
[05:28] Anika Bose: Telemetry must be negotiable; we can't have any telemetry leaving the site, even for errors. Error logs must be stored locally and pulled on-demand during audits.
[05:36] Derek O'Connell: Okay offline-only mode is available. We also support an audit API that produces a signed report you can store in WORM. That meets many compliance use cases.
[05:45] Dr. Saira Khan: What about key rotation? Auditors ask about rotation and proof that old keys were revoked.
[05:51] Priya Raman: Rotation is supported via certificates and manifest versioning. If you run your HSM as the trust root, the verification will fail if keys are revoked. We can provide procedures for key rotation and key compromise playbooks.
[06:05] Leo Zhang: On the hardware side, power per rack is limited. We can't exceed 10kW per cage. Cooling is marginal. If we add A100s we'll need to upgrade PDUs and CRAC units. That has long lead times.
[06:19] Marta Li: Understood — so for pilot we should minimize additional hardware. Could you share the exact GPU SKUs and PDU details, Michael?
[06:26] Michael Reyes: I'll send a spreadsheet with serials, SKUs, PDU circuits, and power headroom.
[06:31] Marta Li: Great. We'll then propose a 3-node pilot that fits existing constraints — maybe use the two A40s you have and one higher-memory rented GPU for benchmarking during pilot if you can do a short-term swap.
[06:44] Dr. Saira Khan: Rented hardware might trigger procurement. Can Redwood provide short-term dedicated instances for benchmarking that we can mirror offline?
[06:51] Marta Li: Yes, we can spin a Redwood Dedicated cluster (hosted) with same model/quantization to run benchmarks and produce latency profiles to extrapolate to your on-prem topology. That will be part of our SOW.
[07:00] Derek O'Connell: Also, we need to discuss model provenance. We sign model weights we ship but you may require that the model training lineage be documented.
[07:08] Anika Bose: We need documentation that ties each model artifact to a training snapshot and release note for validation and reproducibility.
[07:15] Priya Raman: We can provide model manifests including hash, training commit id (if available), and release notes. We'll include that in the signed bundle.
[07:24] Marta Li: Let's capture risk/unknowns: power/CRAC constraints, HSM integration complexity, audit retention length, and model tail-latency on existing GPU SKUs. We'll address each in the pilot plan.
[07:36] Dr. Saira Khan: On SLA — we don't need a public SLA for pilot, but we need runbooks and escalation paths. Also, if an update fails we need rollback options that don't leave the model in a partially updated state.
[07:49] Derek O'Connell: Rollback is handled via snapshot + atomic apply pattern. Our installer takes a preflight snapshot of model artifacts and runtime state; if apply fails we revert. We'll provide the scripts and runbooks.
[08:02] Michael Reyes: Sounds good. What's the expected timeline to get pilot SOW and checklist?
[08:07] Marta Li: We'll send the air-gapped checklist and draft SOW by Tuesday (2027-01-11). After that, if you ok the SOW we can schedule the on-site sizing next week.
[08:16] Anika Bose: We'll review and aim to have compliance feedback in 48 hours.
[08:20] Leo Zhang: I'd like to have a focused on-site call for rack layout and PDU mapping — can we schedule that for next Wednesday?
[08:26] Marta Li: Yes we'll propose times. Derek, any final technical notes?
[08:30] Derek O'Connell: A couple extras — 1) For absence of NVLink, we'll lean on per-request KV cache on disk with warm-up strategies and heavier prefix caching. That affects cold-start latency but keeps memory demands lower. 2) We'll include quantization profiles in the pilot and measure quality/regression against your eval prompts. 3) We'll sign the verification binary; please run it in your staging jump box before production.
[08:55] Michael Reyes: Clarify KV cache on disk — is that safe for PHI? We need encryption at rest and access controls.
[09:02] Priya Raman: Yes encrypted at rest using your KMS/HSM or local disk encryption. Access is RBAC-controlled; we can map to your LDAP.
[09:10] Anika Bose: LDAP integration + SSO is mandatory for operators. SAML or OIDC acceptable?
[09:16] Derek O'Connell: We support SAML and OIDC and can integrate with LDAP for group mapping. We'll provide templates for role mappings.
[09:24] Dr. Saira Khan: Any mention of competitors or market options we looked at? We briefly evaluated EdgeNexus and AstraServe but they lacked airgap documentation. CloudModelCo had an on-prem offering but required outbound check-ins which is a blocker.
[09:37] Marta Li: Thanks. We'll capture that in the notes. Quick recap of next steps: Marta to send checklist & security whitepaper, Derek to produce benchmark plan, Michael to share infra spreadsheet, Anika to send compliance matrix, and schedule on-site sizing.
[09:52] Dr. Saira Khan: That works for us. One last ask — can Redwood include a sample signed audit report so our auditors can pre-approve format?
[09:59] Priya Raman: We'll attach a redacted sample audit package to the checklist.
[10:04] Marta Li: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up over email.
[10:09] Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional misheard acronyms (K-V cash for KV cache earlier in notes), speaker overlap captured as separate lines.
